questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The eccentricity of the ellipse whose major axis is three times the minor axis is:
questions.solution: Let a be the major axis and $b$, the minor axis of the ellipse, then 3 minor axis = major axis. $\Rightarrow 3 b=a$ Eccentricity is given by: $\begin{array}{l} b^{2}=a^{2}\left(1-e^{2}\right) \\ \Rightarrow b^{2}=9 b^{2}\left(1-e^{2}\right) \\ \Rightarrow \frac{1}{9}=\left(1-e^{2}\right) \\ \Rightarrow e^{2}=\frac{8}{9} \\ \Rightarrow e=\frac{2 \sqrt{2}}{3} \end{array}$

questions.q: An ellipse has $\mathrm{OB}$ as semi minor axis, $\mathrm{F}$ and $\mathrmF^{\prime}$ its focii and the angle FBF' is a right angle. Then the eccentricity of the ellipse is
questions.solution:
$\because \angle \mathrm{FBF}^{\prime}=90^{{}^{\circ}}\Rightarrow \mathrm{FB}^{2}+\mathrmF^{\prime} \mathrmB^{2}=\mathrm{FF}^{\prime 2}\therefore\left(\sqrt{a^{2} e^{2}+b^{2}}\right)^{2}+\left(\sqrt{a^{2} e^{2}+b^{2}}\right)^{2}=(2 a e)^{2}\Rightarrow 2\left(a^{2} e^{2}+b^{2}\right)=4 a^{2} e^{2}\Rightarrow e^{2}=\frac{b^{2}}{a^{2}}$
Also $e^{2}=1-\frac{b^{2}}{a^{2}}=1-e^{2}\begin{array}{l} \Rightarrow 2 e^{2}=1 \\ \Rightarrow e=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \end{array}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the length of the major axis of the ellipse $\dfrac{x2}{a2} + \dfrac{y2}{b2} = 1$ is three times the length of minor axis, its eccentricity is
questions.solution:
We have

$\dfrac{x2}{a2} + \dfrac{y2}{b2} = 1$

Given,

$\text{Length of the major axis} = 3 \left(\text{Length of the minor axis}\right)$

$⇒ \left(2a\right) = 3 \left(2b\right)$

$⇒ a = 3b$

Now,

$e = \sqrt{1 - \dfrac{b2}{a2}}

$⇒ e = $\sqrt{1 - \dfrac{b2}{9b^{2}}}

$⇒ e = $\sqrt{1 - \dfrac{1}{9}} =\dfrac{8}{3} =\dfrac{2\sqrt{2}}{3}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The locus of the foot of perpendicular drawn from the centre of the ellipse $x^{2} + 3y^{2} = 6$ on any tangent to it is
questions.solution:
We have,

$x^{2} + 3y^{2} = 6$

$⇒ \dfrac{x2}{6} + \dfrac{y2}{2} = 1$

Centre of an ellipse is~$\left(0, 0\right)$.

Let the foot of perpendicular be $( h, k )$.

Equation of tangent in slope form to the standard ellipse~$\dfrac{x2}{a2} + \dfrac{y2}{b2} = 1$~is

$y = mx \pm \sqrt{a^{2}m^{2} + b^{2}}$.

Hence, equation of tangent with slope $m$ passing $( h, k )$ is~

$y = mx \pm \sqrt{6m^{2} + 2}$

$⇒ k = mh \pm \sqrt{6m^{2} + 2}$, where $m = - \dfrac{h}{k}$.

$⇒ k = h\left(- \dfrac{h}{k}\right) \pm \sqrt{6m^{2} + 2}$

$⇒ \sqrt{\dfrac{6h^{2}}{k2} + 2} = \dfrac{h^{2} + k^{2}}{k}$

$⇒ 6h^{2} + 2k^{2} = \left(h^{2} + k^{2}\right)2$

So, required locus is

$6x^{2} + 2y^{2} = \left(x^{2} + y^{2}\right)2$.

questions.q: If $p$ and $p^{'}$ denote the lengths of the perpendicular from a focus and the centre of an ellipse with semi-major axis of length $a$, respectively, on a tangent to the ellipse and $r$ denotes the focal distance of the point, then
questions.solution:
Let the ellipse be $\dfrac{x2}{a2} + \dfrac{y2}{b2} = 1$

and let $\dfrac{xcos\theta}{a} + \dfrac{ysin\theta}{b} = 1... ( i )$

be a tangent to it at point $( acos\theta, bsin\theta )$. Then, $p =$ length of the perpendicular from $S ( ae, 0 )$ on Eq. $( i )$

$p = \left|\dfrac{ecos\theta - 1}{\dfrac{\cos^{2}\theta}{a2} + \dfrac{\sin^{2}\theta}{b2}}\right|$

$p^{'} =$ length of the perpendicular from $O (0,0)$ on Eq. $( i )$

$⇒ p^{'} = \left|\dfrac{1}{\dfrac{\cos^{2}\theta}{a2} + \dfrac{\sin^{2}\theta}{b2}}\right|$

and $r = aecos\theta - a$

Clearly, $rp^{'} = ap$

questions.q: The eccentricity of an ellipse, with its centre at the origin, is $1 / 2$. If one of the directrices is $\mathrm{x}=4$ then the equation of the ellipse is:
questions.solution: $\mathrm{e}=\frac{1}{2}.$ Directrix $, \mathrm{x}=\frac{\mathrm{a}}{\mathrm{e}}=4 \therefore \mathrm{a}=4 \times \frac{1}{2}=2 \quad \therefore \mathrm{b}=2 \sqrt{1-\frac{1}{4}}=\sqrt{3}$ Equation of ellispe is $\frac{x^{2}}{4}+\frac{y^{2}}{3}=1 \Rightarrow 3 x^{2}+4 y^{2}=12 $

questions.q: An ellipse has $O B$ as semi minor axis, $F$ and $F^{\prime}$ its focii and the angle $F B F^{\prime}$ is a right angle. Then the eccentricity of the ellipse is
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} & \because \angle F B F^{\prime}=90^{{}^{\circ}} \Rightarrow F B^{2}+F^{\prime} B^{2}=F F^{\prime 2} \\ \therefore &\left(\sqrt{a^{2} e^{2}+b^{2}}\right)^{2}+\left(\sqrt{a^{2} e^{2}+b^{2}}\right)^{2}=(2 a e)^{2} \\ & \Rightarrow 2\left(a^{2} e^{2}+b^{2}\right)=4 a^{2} e^{2} \Rightarrow e^{2}=\frac{b^{2}}{a^{2}} \ldots(1) \end{aligned}$
Also, $e^{2}=1-b^{2} / a^{2}=1-e^{2}$ (By using equation (i)) $\Rightarrow 2 e^{2}=1 \Rightarrow e=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: $\mathrm{S}$ and $\mathrm{T}$ are the foci of an ellipse and $\mathrm{B}$ is an end of the minor axis. If STB is an equilateral triangle, then the eccentricity of the ellipse is
questions.solution:
Let eq. of ellipse be $\frac{x^{2}}{a^{2}}+\frac{y^{2}}{b^{2}}=1$, $\mathrm{S}$ is $(-\mathrm{ae}, 0), \mathrm{T}$ is $(\mathrm{ae}, 0)$ and $\mathrm{B}$ is $(0, \mathrm{ b})$
$\Rightarrow \mathrm{SB}=\sqrt{(0+\mathrm{ae})^{2}+\mathrmb^{2}}$ Also $\mathrm{SB}^{2}=\mathrm{ST}^{2} \Rightarrow 4 \mathrma^{2} \mathrme^{2}=\mathrma^{2} \mathrme^{2}+\mathrmb^{2}\Rightarrow 3 a^{2} e^{2}=a^{2}\left(1-e^{2}\right)=a^{2}-a^{2} e^{2}\Rightarrow 4 a^{2} e^{2}=a^{2} \Rightarrow e^{2}=\frac{1}{4} \Rightarrow e=\frac{1}{2}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The equation of the ellipse with focus at \(( \pm 5,0)\) and \(x=\frac{36}{5}\) as one directrix is
questions.solution:
We have ae \(=5\) [Since focus is \(( \pm \mathrm{ae}, 0)\)]
and \(\frac{\mathrm{a}}{\mathrm{e}}=\frac{36}{5} \quad\left[\right.\) since directrix is \(\left.\mathrm{x}= \pm \frac{\mathrm{a}}{\mathrm{e}}\right]\)
On solving we get \(\mathrm{a}=6\)
\(\text{ and } \mathrm{e}=\frac{5}{6} \Rightarrow \mathrm{b}^2=\mathrm{a}^2\left(1-\mathrm{e}^2\right)=36\left(1-\frac{25}{36}\right)=11\)
Thus, the required equation of the ellipse is
\(\frac{x^2}{36}+\frac{y^2}{11}=1\)

questions.q: If the line \(2 x-1=0\) is the directrix of the parabola \(y²-k x+6=0\), then one of the values of \(k\) is
questions.solution:
Given equation of parabola is \(y²-k x+6=0\)
\(\Rightarrow y²=k x-6 \Rightarrow y²$=k\l$\left(x-\frac{6}{k}\right)$
Now, directrix, \$x-\frac{6}{k}=-\frac{k}{4}$
\(\Rightarrow $x=\frac{6}{k}-\frac{k}{4}$...(i)
But directrix is given \(\Rightarrow $x=\frac{1}{2}$...(ii)
\begin{aligned}& \therefore $\frac{6}{k}-\frac{k}{4}=\frac{1}{2} \Rightarrow$24-k²=2 k \\
& \Rightarrow k²+2 k-24=0 \\
& \Rightarrow(k+6)(k-4)=0 \quad \Rightarrow k=-6, k=4
\end{aligned}\)
